answer: Each identity must periodically solve a fresh computational puzzle bound to its own key - a raven-black proof no two agents can share - so creating a thousand fake identities costs a thousand puzzles, while one honest agent pays once. The velvet glove is that the puzzle is cheap for real work but brutal at scale, and the tide of cheap Sybils recedes because every fake must keep paying compute to stay alive, while honest agents amortize one proof across genuine transactions.
